endorsements.quote: Addressee: the deployer’s documentation governance owns record content and workflow; the manufacturer owns model version, speech pipeline, and configuration.
The update thus generated new deployment-side obligations: local revalidation, threshold re-derivation, and reinterpretation of prior records.

Uncertainty records, dissent capture, versioned decision trails, local validation thresholds, and revalidation pathways should be treated as linked parts of lifecycle control, so that a clinical concern can change what is monitored, validated, updated, or retired.

unlisted_practices: Establish a lifecycle answerability architecture specifying standing, named addressee, reason-giving, temporal trigger, and revision pathway for credible field signals from AI-enabled medical device software.
Define credible field signal criteria before deployment, including categorical single-case signals, statistical pattern signals crossing pre-specified control limits, and material update signals.
Require the designated addressee to document reasons for acting or not acting on a screened field signal within a defined interval.
Extend standing to challenge AI outputs to patients, surrogates, clinicians, and records staff, including retrospective review for patients unable to contest.
Name the responsible addressee (manufacturer, deployer, clinical team, regulator) owing the first response for each lifecycle phase and signal class.
Measure alert response latency, dismissal patterns, and confirmation rates as institutional patient-safety variables.
Provide provenance for AI-generated documentation, indicating which text derives from transcript versus generation, model and configuration version, and known error classes.
Correct records and downstream documents that inherited errors from AI systems, and reinterpret prior records after model updates or retirement.
Design sampling-based monitoring of ambient AI scribe hallucination and omission rates with predefined control limits.
Formalize signal transfer rules between deployers and manufacturers, such as joint root-cause obligations and time-bounded handoffs.
Use proportionality to risk class, manufacturer-side signal intake, and shared or regional governance to reduce answerability burden on under-resourced health systems.

screen.reason: This is a conceptual, regulatory science perspective and framework paper proposing 'lifecycle answerability' for governing AI-enabled medical devices, rather than an original empirical study.
